headline: 3 arrested after Salman Muqtadir’s studio attacked and looted
summary: Police say the attack on the content creator's studio and a nearby property was likely triggered by a land dispute.
details: Content creator Salman Muqtadir’s studio and the nearby New Guinea Properties in South Manikdi, Dhaka, were attacked and vandalized by a group of armed individuals on Saturday night.
Witnesses claim over 100 masked men arrived in several pickup vans, firing shots and causing widespread destruction.
The attackers reportedly broke CCTV cameras, assaulted several people, and looted valuables from the housing project office, with authorities claiming approximately 1 crore BDT was stolen.
Dhaka Metropolitan Police (DMP) Joint Commissioner Mohidul Islam confirmed that three people have been arrested in connection with the incident.
According to the police, the attack is suspected to have been motivated by a land dispute involving the building owner.
Joint Commissioner Mohidul Islam stated that while the identities of the suspects have not yet been fully confirmed, all those involved will be brought to justice quickly.
caption:
Over 100 masked men in pickup vans attacked Salman Muqtadir’s studio and a nearby property, looting 1 crore BDT.

Content creator Salman Muqtadir’s studio and the nearby New Guinea Properties in South Manikdi, Dhaka, were attacked and vandalized by a group of armed individuals on Saturday night.

Witnesses claim over 100 masked men arrived in several pickup vans, firing shots and causing widespread destruction.

The attackers reportedly broke CCTV cameras, assaulted several people, and looted valuables from the housing project office, with authorities claiming approximately 1 crore BDT was stolen.

Dhaka Metropolitan Police (DMP) Joint Commissioner Mohidul Islam confirmed that three people have been arrested in connection with the incident.

According to the police, the attack is suspected to have been motivated by a land dispute involving the building owner.

Joint Commissioner Mohidul Islam stated that while the identities of the suspects have not yet been fully confirmed, all those involved will be brought to justice quickly.

headline_marked: Mirpur health centre attack: [[Shah Ali Police Station OC withdrawn]]
headline: Mirpur health centre attack: Shah Ali Police Station OC withdrawn
summary: The officer-in-charge of Shah Ali Police Station was removed from his post following an attack and looting of a health centre in Mirpur-1.
details: The officer-in-charge (OC) of Shah Ali Police Station, Jahangir Alam, has been withdrawn from his post on administrative grounds.
The move follows an attack on the Radda MCH-FP Centre in Mirpur-1 on Thursday night, where a group of people vandalised the facility and looted valuables.
DMP Commissioner Mosleh Uddin Ahmed visited the centre and ordered an investigation into whether there was any police negligence or failure during the incident.
A committee was formed to the investigate the attack, and the Mirpur Division Deputy Commissioner confirmed that the report has been submitted.
Jahangir Alam has been attached to the Central Reserve Office of the Headquarters and Administration Department of Dhaka Metropolitan Police.
Police have already arrested nine people in connection with the attack and looting at the NGO-run health centre.
caption:
A police chief is out after a health centre was looted in Mirpur.

The officer-in-charge (OC) of Shah Ali Police Station, Jahangir Alam, has been withdrawn from his post on administrative grounds.

The move follows an attack on the Radda MCH-FP Centre in Mirpur-1 on Thursday night, where a group of people vandalised the facility and looted valuables.

DMP Commissioner Mosleh Uddin Ahmed visited the centre and ordered an investigation into whether there was any police negligence or failure during the incident.

A committee was formed to the investigate the attack, and the Mirpur Division Deputy Commissioner confirmed that the report has been submitted.

Jahangir Alam has been attached to the Central Reserve Office of the Headquarters and Administration Department of Dhaka Metropolitan Police.

Police have already arrested nine people in connection with the attack and looting at the NGO-run health centre.
